## Critical fixes

- **Codex keeps recording after claude-mem updates** (#6058, thanks @wiesenthal). Codex approves a hook that ships inside a plugin against a fingerprint of the plugin's whole folder. Every claude-mem update rewrites that folder, so after every update Codex switched all seven claude-mem hooks off ("plugin contents changed; hook approval required") and Codex sessions stopped being saved, with no message. The installer now registers claude-mem's Codex hooks in your own `~/.codex/hooks.json`,

## Critical fixes

- **Gemini CLI on Windows records again** (#6079, thanks @tanishqbaweja). On Windows, Gemini CLI runs hook commands through PowerShell. The hook commands claude-mem wrote started with a quoted path, which PowerShell rejects as a parser error. Every claude-mem Gemini hook (SessionStart, BeforeAgent, AfterTool, AfterAgent, SessionEnd) failed on every event since 15.18.0, so Gemini sessions on Windows saved nothing and got no saved context. Hook commands on Windows now start with PowerShell'

- **The worker no longer fails to start when the database is busy at startup** (#6041). If the My Work refresh record was left as "running" by a restart and the database was locked at that moment, the repair write threw and took down the worker's whole startup, so memory stayed off until the next restart. The repair failure is now logged, and the next scheduled check tries again (whether or not scheduled refresh is on).

## eve agents get the same memory as Claude Code and Codex

`claude-mem/eve` now gives an eve agent the full claude-mem memory loop through your cmem.ai account (#6042).

- **Session context:** each turn starts with the recent timeline from your memory. It is refreshed every turn under one message id, so it replaces itself instead of piling up.
- **Recall each turn:** one search before the turn, as before.
- **Recording is now on by default.** After each completed turn the provider sends the prompt, one obs
- **Sync:** a pulled page of synced records waits for another writer instead of failing at once with "database is locked", so a large first pull no longer backs off for minutes (#5996).

## New: claude-mem memory for eve agents

- **`claude-mem/eve`** is a new export of the `claude-mem` npm package. It is a memory provider for [eve](https://eve.dev), Vercel's framework for durable backend agents. An eve agent can now recall what you did in Claude Code, Codex and your other claude-mem clients, using your [cmem.ai](https://cmem.ai) memory (key from cmem.ai/pro/key) (#5863).
  - **Recall:** one search before every turn. No inference spend. Matches reach the model as escaped data, never as inst

## Critical fix

- **Manual saves work again in projects with older manual sessions.** In v15.16.0, `save_memory` (and `POST /api/memory/save`) returned HTTP 500 with `UNIQUE constraint failed: sdk_sessions.memory_session_id` in any project whose manual session was created before 15.16.0 with an older session ID shape. Every save in that project failed. claude-mem now finds and reuses that older session instead of trying to create a duplicate. Deleted sessions still get a fresh ID, as in 15.16.0 (#5842).

## New

- **My Work refresh on your API provider (opt-in):** set `CLAUDE_MEM_WORK_VIEW_AGENT=api` to run the My Work refresh on the provider you already selected (`openrouter`, `openai-compatible`, or the legacy `cmem` spelling). Installs with no logged-in Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI (for example OpenCode or DSH hosts) can now use My Work. With an API provider selected and the setting empty, the refresh no longer falls back to a logged-in Claude Code: no agent runs and nothing is spent until you choose

## Critical fix

- **Antigravity no longer denies every tool call after an upgrade from 14.x (#5670):** an in-place upgrade from an older install left a `PreToolUse` hook (and a `PreInvocation` context hook) in `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`. agy kept firing it before every tool call, the current adapter answered with no decision, and agy denied every call until you re-ran install. Now the Antigravity installer finds those stale entries and migrates the file in place with the same merge install performs. It

## No replay after an outage

When the worker was down or refused a capture, some capture paths kept that work and sent it again later, which could start model calls nobody asked for. They now drop what the worker refused and carry on with new work (#5663):

- **Transcript capture:** a transcript line the worker refuses or cannot take is skipped. Before, the watcher stopped at that line and, once the worker was back, sent it again with every line after it. A restart no longer resends lines from an outage ei

- **A JSON key ending with `_` no longer makes `toCamel` and `toPascal` throw** (#1313). With `transform: postgres.camel`, such a key made the whole query throw. The trailing `_` is now kept, so `a_` stays `a_`, and an empty key stays empty instead of becoming `undefined`.
https://github.com/porsager/postgres/compare/v4.1.0...v4.1.1

- **Node.js 18** is supported again: `engines` is `>=18` and CI runs it. Nothing in Postgres.js needs 20; `using`, `await using` and tracing are used where the runtime has them. Loading it with `require` still needs Node.js 20.19 or 22.12.
- **`PGSSLMODE` is read** (#1307). It was ignored, so `PGSSLMODE=verify-full` connected in plain text without an error. This may change how existing setups connect: `require` now uses TLS and fails against a server without it, and `verify-ca` and `verify-full` check the c

- **A NUL character in a connection parameter can no longer add parameters** (also in v3). A `database`, `user` or `connection` value such as `'db\0user\0postgres'` was sent as further startup parameters, so an app that put untrusted input there, as with a database per tenant, could be made to log in as another user where that user needs no password, or with `replication` or `options` set. A NUL in any protocol string, also in query text and identifiers, now rejects with `NUL_CHARACTER`.

# Version 1.1.0 revision notes

This additive post-acquisition supplement publishes 32 earlier unpublished supporting syscall trials within the same study. Their 28 September 2026 collection dates and four separate eight-trial denominators are explicit. They remain pilot evidence, never pooled with the registered campaign.

The manuscript now states acquisition timestamps relative to registration, maps each family to its acquisition filesystem, highlights the 0/40 ACK-marker dependent-prefix result and the

The complete evidence ZIP contains 930 assignments, 929 result records and 925 eligible endpoint oracles. The four unknown endpoints and one premeasurement slot remain preserved. Original scientific records were copied byte-for-byte, and all 95 cells and 43 registered comparisons were independently recomputed before publication. Prior pilots, qualification observations, full disk images, credentials and private transfer maps are excluded. Dependent log-prefix reconstructions add zero scientific units.

- **Security checks:** warnings for unsupported PHP, Node, Python and database versions, and a Security tab that checks project packages for known vulnerabilities.
- **Migration guard:** OLS saves a project's database before running a migration. **Rewind** puts it back.
- **Services sleep when unused:** MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB and Memcached can stop when idle and wake on connection. Off by default.
- **Database per Git branch:** each branch gets its own database copy.
- **Pull a server database*

- **Dockerize a project:** makes a Dockerfile, compose file and `.dockerignore` for PHP, Node, Python, Go, Rust, Ruby, Java, .NET or static projects. The project is copied into the image, `docker compose watch` keeps it in sync while you edit, and a Production mode builds a small non-root image. OLS also adds the services it detects (database, Redis, queue, mail, search) as pinned images with generated passwords. It shows everything first and never overwrites. Also in the right-click menu of Projects and Si

- **Import databases report:** when an import finishes you get a message, your selection is cleared, and a report lists every database as imported, skipped or failed, with the reason. Copy the report or save it as a text file. It never includes passwords.
- **PHP extensions (PECL)** install only when OLS knows the file's SHA-256: apcu, redis, igbinary, imagick, mongodb, xdebug, pcov and yaml for PHP 8.1–8.5.
